title: World War Two Adventure
welcome_lead: From 1939 to 1945, Britain fought Nazi Germany. The Blitz, evacuation, D-Day — let's walk through WW2. ✈️
meta_desc: WW2 Adventure — a KS3 History walkthrough of the Second World War, the Blitz, and D-Day.
final_note: You met Churchill, the Blitz, evacuation and D-Day — and saw how WW2 reshaped Britain and the world.

concepts.def: Moving children from cities to safer areas

walkthroughs.body_html:
After WW1 Germany was punished by the Treaty of Versailles. The country was angry and poor.

In 1933 Adolf Hitler and the Nazi Party came to power. He built up the army, took over Austria and Czechoslovakia, and then invaded Poland on 1 September 1939.

Britain and France declared war on 3 September 1939. ⚠️

walkthroughs.h2: The Blitz and the Home Front
walkthroughs.body_html:
In 1940, German planes bombed British cities night after night — the Blitz. London, Coventry and many ports were badly hit.

To keep them safe, around 1.5 million children were sent from cities to the countryside — called evacuation.

People used gas masks, blackouts and Anderson shelters. The Prime Minister, Winston Churchill, gave famous speeches: 'We shall fight on the beaches...'. 🇬🇧

In 1940, RAF pilots won the Battle of Britain, stopping a German invasion.

In 1941 Germany attacked the USSR, and Japan attacked the USA — both joined against Hitler.

On D-Day, 6 June 1944, Allied troops landed in Normandy, France. Less than a year later, Germany surrendered. The war in Europe ended on VE Day, 8 May 1945.
